title: Northwind SupplyChain — Prompt Quality & Deployment Field Notes
content:
Summary:
- Quick capture from 2025-06-11 customer sync (Northwind SupplyChain). High-level: they want a deployed on‑prem/private instance to run document summarization + troubleshooting assistant across their warehouse operations. Focus: prompt quality, hallucination mitigation, and consistent latency under bursts from handheld scanners.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (Redwood SE)
- Ethan Porter (Redwood Solutions Eng)
- Priya Nambiar (Northwind SRE)
- Marco Alvarez (Northwind Ops)
- Laura Kim (Northwind Product)

Context / goals:
- Pilot to run at 5 warehouses, ~200 concurrent handheld clients at peak.
- Workloads: short incident summaries (10–50 tokens generated), guided troubleshooting workflows (50–250 tokens), occasional longer analysis tasks (~500 tokens).
- Data constraints: PII present in logs, must stay on‑prem; customer needs KMS integration and audit logs retained 12 months.

Hard requirements (explicit):
- Private deployment (VPC or air‑gapped option) with HSM/KMS key management.
- Model pinning + rollout control: want canary AB test (5% traffic) then ramp.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 220ms for short summaries (10–50 tokens) under expected load.
- Cost target for pilot: keep per-1000-token serving cost < $X (they gave target range; follow up to get exact).
- Auditability: token-level usage logs + per-request metadata (route, model-version, prompt-id).

Non-functional concerns we flagged:
- KV cache efficacy: short-turn prompts reuse prefixes; suggest aggressive prefix caching. But handhelds sometimes send slightly noisy prefixes (timestamp, device-id) — need normalization.
- Batching: prefer latency-first minimal batching for summaries; can use larger batching for longer analyses.
- Quantization: customer worried about quality drop on quantized LLM; propose A/B on quantization profile + quality eval on prompt set.
- Fallback policy: define fallback to smaller model when Primary overloaded, but must preserve hallucination risk profile.

Gotchas / observed pain points (from call):
- Their current proto (local rule-based) loses context when steps include device logs with stack traces — LLM hallucinations cause incorrect root cause attributions.
- DeviceID/date tokens appended to beginning of prompts break similarity caching and metric grouping.
- Their network egress is restricted; private control plane with agent approach preferred over outbound-only managed control plane.

Prompt quality notes (examples from customer):
- Example 1 (summaries): "Scanner 12 error: dropcount mismatch at 2025-06-09 13:01. Stack: io.read->fifo->index 4032.\nGoal: single sentence root-cause + confidence 0–100."
  - Expected output style: very terse, reference relevant log lines (one-liner), include confidence.
  - Failure modes: hallucinated cause ("firmware bug") when logs only show buffer overflow.

- Example 2 (troubleshoot flow): "Step list to diagnose intermittent barcode read failures when worker reports ~3% false negatives. Provide 3 checks, each with command/expected output and timeframe."
  - Expect structured steps with commands that run on their local diagnostic agent.

Quality mitigation suggestions we proposed (technical):
- Add explicit "do not invent" guard rails in system prompt + numbered evidence extraction step.
- Use retrieval augmentation: attach the last 3 device logs (normalized) as context; enforce token budget.
- Use Redwood Optimize to generate recommended batching & quantization profiles per-workload (short summary vs deep analysis).
- Set up evaluation harness: holdout prompt set (50 exemplars per workload) and automated regression alerts on metric regressions (exactness, hallucination rate).

Operational considerations:
- Autoscale policy: keep headroom for 2x burst (200 -> 400 concurrent short requests) with warm KV cache to hit latency SLO.
- Canary rollout suggested: 5% for 24h, compare token cost, latency p95, hallucination metric.
- Logging: token-level cost + model-version tag; customer will need a daily export to their SIEM (S3/GCS endpoint internal).

Security & compliance:
- KMS: customer wants HSM-backed key in their vault. Red team asked for TDE and audit log integrity — follow up with security team to confirm options.
- Data retention: logs 12 months, but customer asked for ability to purge per-request on-demand. Need to confirm API support for deletions.

Action items / next steps:
- [Maya] Create a short evaluation prompt set (50 items) by 2025-06-16. Attach to JIRA NW-317.
- [Ethan] Draft quantization A/B plan (profile options + expected quality delta) by 2025-06-19.
- [Samir] Confirm private control plane deployment model options (VPC peering vs agent vs fully air-gapped) and constraints; include network diagram by 2025-06-18.
- [Northwind: Priya] Provide sample device logs (anonymized) and current rule-based output mapping by 2025-06-15 (they committed).
- [Redwood Security] Clarify KMS/HSM integration checklist and deletion API availability; expected by 2025-06-20.

Open questions to resolve (for next meeting):
- Exact cost target per-1000 tokens they referenced — need number to optimize configs.
- Are handhelds able to do offline batching (buffering) for larger analyses during low network times? If yes, we can change batching strategy.
- Do they require full air‑gapped (no outbound) or is a narrow outbound-control-plane acceptable?

Evaluation / metrics proposal (quick):
- Short summaries: exactness score (match to gold root cause), hallucination rate, p95 latency.
- Troubleshoot flow: step correctness (binary per-step), helpfulness (human-rated 1–5), average token cost.

Notes to self (informal):
- Normalize device id + timestamps before caching to improve prefix hit-rate (preprocessor on agent).
- Consider a lightweight prompt templating library on customer side to keep variability low.
- Suggest local small model (low-cost) as first pass classifier to triage (if noisy prompt then route to larger model).

Reference links (for team):
- Redwood Optimize guide (internal): confluence://redwood/optimize-guide (placeholder)
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-agent#PR-482

Meeting cadence: weekly until pilot launch (tentative launch window: late July). Next sync: 2025-06-19 (confirm).

-- end of scratchpad --
